newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: INJUNCTION HALTS DUTCH NAM GAS DRILLING PLANS.
newsitem.headline: INJUNCTION HALTS DUTCH NAM GAS DRILLING PLANS.

text.p: An environmental group in the north of the Netherlands on Monday won a temporary injunction to prevent Nederlandse Aardolie Maatschappij (NAM) from drilling in the North Sea off the Dutch Wadden Islands.
The local environmental body, the Waddenvereiniging, won the injunction at a court in the Friesian town of Leeuwarden. The court should produce a substantive ruling latar.

"The court found that the decision (to allow drilling) was unsound.... Our experience also shows that these preliminary rulings normally lead to a success conclusion," Jan Veltman, a lawyer at the Waddenvereiniging, told Reuters.
NAM -- jointly owned by Royal Dutch/Shell and Exxon -- received permission last November from the Ministry of Economic Affairs to start test drilling in the area from May 1.
Earlier this month, the ministry also granted NAM permission to test for gas at five sites in the ecologically sensitive Wadden Sea, between the Dutch mainland and the Wadden Islands.
The Waddenvereiniging plans to prevent NAM from drilling.
"It is not economically necessary and would cause great ecological disturbance," Veltman said.
No-one at NAM was immediately available for comment.
The Ministry of Economic Affairs said the court ruling would not lead to an immediate review of its policy of granting permission to drill offshore.
"We have to study what was said today, but really we must wait for the final (court) ruling," a ministry spokeswoman said.
